convoLines.text: "Teach me something. Anything you know that I don't. Seen worse."
"All right. Show me when we work together."
"I'd like to learn something I can use today. Show me while you work, when you have a moment."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on teaching them something."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Just... be straight with me."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I wasn't an exterminator. I was a Dentist. The less of me is out there, the less can be used against me."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Can I tell you something? I have been lying about my age — I'm younger than I look."
Harold has an edge today — something curdled.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what they confided."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Sam always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I clean up other people's messes quietly. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I walked the whole perimeter twice. It's fine. Everything's fine. I'm not fine."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Meet me at where the staghorn sumac grows thick and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"About that question — Where are you from — originally? Before all this. I really mean that."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Honestly, I really think — Still on where you're from."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Simple as that."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Sam owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Sam said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we got cut off, 4 days back. 'Okay. We'll pick this up later.'"
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Nobody says Sam's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"I clean up other people's messes quietly for Sam, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Cattail — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on what scares you most."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "2 of us are down with a wringing-out sickness. Boil everything. I mean everything."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"My part? I carry water to the sick row. Someone has to."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never did finish talking about what they confided — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? '...Anyway. What did you want to ask?'"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what they confided. That's still where we are."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Have you seen the sick row? 2 down with a wringing-out sickness. Nobody says it out loud but everyone's counting."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "2 of us are down with a wringing-out sickness. Boil everything. I mean everything."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Wash your hands. I say it ten times a day now. Wash your hands."
"If it takes anyone else we bury them properly. That's the deal we made."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Jerome sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. I hate to ask this, but whatever this is, it's getting worse — I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Can you do anything?"
"Rest and clean water aren't cutting it. If this turns, I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. I need someone who knows what they're doing."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The Tide Clock. They just... took Vasyl. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I tried the Lamb's Quarters like you showed me. Didn't poison anyone, so that's a win."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
On the way, Harold stops and actually teaches you something — how they read a slope for water, how their grandmother did it. (Knowledge, freely given. The Codex notes it.)
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Vasyl — The Tide Clock, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
You told me you're from Columbus, Ohio. Do you think about it much?
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Between us — Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"

"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you heard what they're calling Sweeps Week? Jerome is pushing 'Big-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. I wanted to ask rather than assume."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Alright. Catch you later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started. Anyway — how are YOU doing?"
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"I don't keep score on that. Score-keeping is how you stop sleeping. I do what the day needs and I don't rehearse it after."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.

"Okay." Olivia looks down. "Okay, you got me. I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to make the System explain itself. I wanted an edge. You were new, you were listening, and I used it. I'm not proud of that." Their voice is small.
"That again?" Olivia sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Can I tell you something? I'm saving a candy bar for when things get better. I haven't told anyone."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Jerome shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what they confided."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Vasyl and Rafael — Hollow Belly, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You told me yes, once. No details. I haven't forgotten. I just don't ask."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Yeah? What's up? Just... be straight with me."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Hollow Belly. They just... took Vasyl and Rafael. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I check the treeline every hour. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never did finish talking about what they confided — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? '...Anyway. What did you want to ask?' We still owe what's been happening a proper ending, too."
They settle in like someone glad you're here.
"As I said — Still on what they confided."
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Hardened The Secret Deck. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone?"
"I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"I go to the treeline edge and count my breaths. Ten of them. That's my alone. Then I come back — alone is a luxury, and also a little bit a lie."
"Still on needing to be alone."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took you — Hardened The Secret Deck, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.

deathBeat: d13: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Sam Tkachenko is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d13: 🕯️ Sam Tkachenko is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d14: That night, they bring Sam home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d13: At the grave, Jerome speaks for Karl — "Sam trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d13: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d13: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."
d13: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "AUDIENCE EXPANSION! Your party cap is now FOUR! The people demanded bigger ensembles! Don't let us down!"
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "A viewer sent this. A FAN. We checked. It is not dinner." A pause. "We checked twice. The fans are very insistent that you open it ON CAMERA."
d15: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 38. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 3."
d15: SYSTEM: Quest protocol integrated. Objectives will appear.
burialWindowSay: d13: At the grave, Jerome speaks for Karl — "Sam trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d14: That night, they bring Sam home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d15: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+4 integration)
d15: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+3 integration)
d16: You say a few words for Sam. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d16: You bury Sam. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
echoSample: d16: "Sam always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d20: "Huh. Let me think about that." "Sam owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
d20: "I keep turning over the last thing Sam said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
d20: "Nobody says Sam's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
d20: "I clean up other people's messes quietly for Sam, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
echoV2Sample: d16: The village raises a marker by the fire — Sam, day 16. the wild. A place to stand.
echoV2DeltaSample: d16: The village raises a marker by the fire — Sam, day 16. the wild. A place to stand.

lastSay: d84: ◈ WORD TRAVELS — riders from The Red Table III bring talk of Haven. Out there they call you the Feared. The show's narration lingers on your hands.
d84: Snow by morning. (-8°C — Freezing) The ground goes iron — forage thin, walking dear.
d84: Jerome Mikhailov reads the sky: clear tomorrow, freezing.
d84: The cold works on everyone — the village wakes aching from the deep cold.
d84: Dawn. You wake rested. (+0 health, energy restored. By the fire. Good enough.)
